message.content:
**Uno – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | How it works | |---------|---------------|--------------| | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (Red, Yellow, Green, Blue). Each color has numbers 0‑9 (two of each 1‑9, one 0) and two of each action card: Skip, Reverse, Draw Two. Plus 4 Wild cards and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | Shuffle the deck and deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down to form the draw pile. Turn the top card over to start the discard pile. | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or a pre‑agreed total). Points are tallied after each round. | | **Gameplay** | 1. Play proceeds clockwise (unless a Reverse changes direction). 2. On your turn, you may play **one** card that matches either the color, number, or symbol of the top discard. 3. If you cannot play, you must draw one card from the draw pile. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately; otherwise, your turn ends. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – next player loses their turn.
• **Reverse** – changes play direction.
• **Draw Two** – next player draws two cards and loses their turn.
• **Wild** – you choose the new color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – you choose the new color; next player draws four cards and loses their turn. (Can only be played if you have no other playable card; otherwise, the opponent can challenge.) | | **Calling “Uno”** | When you have **exactly one card left**, you must say “UNO!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player catches you, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards their last card. That player scores points equal to the sum of the values of all cards remaining in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20 points, Wild/Wild Draw Four = 50 points. | | **Scoring** | Add the round score to the winner’s total. Play continues until someone reaches the target score (usually 500). | | **Variations** | • **Stacking** – allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing.
• **Custom rules** – e.g., “Draw Two” can be played on any card, not just matching color/number. | **Quick Tips** - Keep an eye on what colors your opponents are avoiding; that can hint at what they hold. - Use Wild cards strategically to change the color when you’re stuck. - Remember the “UNO” rule—failure to call it can cost you two cards! Enjoy the fast‑paced, colorful fun of Uno!
